## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 53, entitled *Gaṇaparibhāsana* ("Reviling the community"), belongs to the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga of the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The core rule stipulates that a nun who in anger reviles or intimidates a group of nuns commits an offense entailing expiation (*yā pana bhikkhunī caṇḍīkatā gaṇaṁ paribhāseyya, pācittiyaṁ*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. There is no corresponding rule in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga [Hüsken 1997].
In the origin story, the nun Thullanandā criticizes the community of nuns over legal decisions concerning the suspended nun Caṇḍakālī, sharing thematic and narrative parallels with Bhikkhunī Saṅghādisesa 4 [Hüsken 1997]. Together with the *padabhājanīya* (word commentary), the rule serves fundamentally as a prohibition against criticizing legally valid monastic procedures and decisions, while also broadly forbidding the reviling or snubbing of fellow nuns [Hüsken 1997]. The casuistry specifies that reviling several nuns, a single nun, or an unordained person incurs an offense of wrong conduct (*dukkaṭa*), while exceptions apply if comments occur in the context of canonical recitation or exposition [Hüsken 1997]. English translations include one by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the corresponding rule in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, the Bhikkhunī Parivāra (Pācittiya 53), as well as Bhikṣuṇī Vinaya texts preserved in Tibetan (Mūlasarvāstivāda) and Chinese translations across the Dharmaguptaka, Sarvāstivāda, and Mahīśāsaka recensions [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus independently confirms cross-language alignment with the Tibetan Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga (D0005) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus identifies shared passages across 95 texts, displaying particularly extensive reuse with Bhikkhunī Saṅghādisesa 4 (§1.1–1.18), various other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga pācittiyas (such as Pc 26, Pc 27, and Pc 30), and the Khandhakas (Vattakkhandhaka and Mahākhandhaka) [DharmaNexus].
